chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah and Ali ibn Khalid from Abdul Karim ibn Amr from Amr ibn al-Bara' said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Our companions are saying that if a man divorces a woman once or a hundred times, it is only one (divorce). And it had reached us from you and from your forefathers (peace be upon them) that they were saying: if he divorces once or a hundred times, it is only one.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is as it has reached you.'
ai.seo_question: Does pronouncing divorce multiple times count as one or three divorces in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the Shia jurisprudential stance on *Talaq Raj'i* (revocable divorce), affirming that multiple pronouncements made in a single sitting or context constitute only one divorce, countering the view that each utterance counts separately. Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) validates the consensus of his companions and predecessors, establishing a precedent for interpreting the intent behind the words rather than merely the quantity of utterances. This ruling is pivotal in Shia *Fiqh* for determining the waiting period (*Iddah*) and the conditions for remarriage without a new contract.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Ja’far Bin Sama’at, and Ali Bin Halid, from Abdul Kareem Bin Amro, from Amro Bin Al Bara’a who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Our companions are saying that the man, when he divorces a woman once, or a hundred times, but rather it is one, and it had reached us from you<sup>asws</sup>, and from your<sup>asws</sup> forefathers<sup>asws</sup> that they<sup>asws</sup> were saying: ‘When a divorce is one, or one hundred times, but rather it is one’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is just as it has reached you’.
en.sarwar: 4. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from Ja‘far ibn Sama‘ah and Ali ibn Khalid from ‘Abd al-Karim ibn ‘Amr from ‘Amr ibn al-Bara’ who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Our people say that if one divorces (pronounces the expression for divorce) his wife once or one hundred times it counts only one divorce.’ It has been narrated to us from you that your ancestors, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, have stated this Hadith. ‘If one divorces his wife (at one time and place) once or one hundred times it counts only one divorce.” He (the Imam) said, ‘It is just as it is narrated to you.””
